newsitem.title: UK: UK govt to back wait-and-see policy on EMU - paper.
newsitem.headline: UK govt to back wait-and-see policy on EMU - paper.

text.p: The British cabinet will back Prime Minister John Major's wait-and-see policy on a European single currency on Thursday, the Financial Times reported.
Such a decision, based on a briefing paper issued by the Treasury, would put an end to argument about whether the government will harden its policy before the election.

An unnamed minister was quoted by the newspaper as saying the briefing paper "completely underpins everything that the prime minister and the chancellor have been saying, that there will be no opportunity to take a firm view on whether or not to join a single currency until after the general election."

Major, lagging in polls and dogged by party splits over Europe, must call an election by May at the latest. The splits flared up again in the last few weeks with reports of divisions between Major and Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke.

But the newspaper reported that leading Eurosceptics, like former cabinet minister John Redwood, who quit the cabinet last year to challenge Major for the party leadership, had decided to tone down calls for a tougher policy on the single currency.
The decision to calm down their public campaign is a sign they have accepted there is little chance of changing government policy in the run-up to the election, it said.

The briefing paper put the seal on this, the newspaper said, saying there was no way a judgement could be made on whether countries were joining a single currency on the basis of "fudged" criteria until at least nine months after the election.
